messages:
Neha (oncall): Noticed a recurring p95 regression on generation-api at 22:15 UTC during nightly traffic bursts. Looks like the same backpressure pattern from last month; opening a thread to decide SLO handling + owners.

Diego: Traces show queue spikes on the preprocessor shard and fallback to slower CPUs. Multi-tenant promo traffic again, not a single customer.

Hannah: Can we avoid global SLO drift by using a temporary regulation window per-route? Suggest marking affected routes with a 48h soft-target and avoid counting into monthly error budget.

Anoop: I can own the autoscale tweak (lower CPU pct -> scale earlier) and add the preproc queue metric to runbook. ETA: 6h.

Neha (oncall): Hannah, can you handle the SLO dashboard note + statuspage blurb? Include Dedicated opt-out flag. ETA: 2h.

Hannah: Will do. Draft: "Temporary p95 target for /v1/generate increased to 600ms for 48h due to recurring preprocessor saturation. Dedicated customers may opt-out; contact support."

Diego: I'll add a prefix cache panel and a token-size histogram to the ops dashboard. ETA: 4h.

Neha (oncall): Ops-Bot, please create ticket and subtasks for autoscale, SLO comms, cache panel, and a follow-up RFC for route-specific fallback.

Ops-Bot: Created ticket REDW-3742 with subtasks REDW-3743 -> Anoop (autoscale), REDW-3744 -> Hannah (SLO comms), REDW-3745 -> Diego (dash panels), REDW-3746 -> Neha (fallback RFC). Due dates assigned.

Neha (oncall): Agree to mark the 48h window as "maintenance override" if we capture justification in the postmortem. Scheduling 48h check-in: 1777857634. Please update tickets as progress happens.

Hannah: SLO note posted, linking status: https://status.redwood.dev/incidents/REDW-3742

Anoop: Autoscale tweak deployed to canary; monitoring.

Diego: Panels live; initial cache-hit reading 32% during spike.

Neha (oncall): Thanks team, attaching this thread to the incident postmortem. Closing for async follow-up.
